results.name: Orientation Removal
results.description: Nullify orientation assignments; check if selector effect disappears.
results.outcome_note: Variance narrowing was destroyed, confirming orientation sensitivity.

results.name: Orientation Randomization
results.description: Scramble orientation independently of residue; check if variance narrows.
results.outcome_note: Variance narrowing was destroyed, confirming orientation sensitivity.

results.name: Residue Dominance
results.description: Attempt to explain entire selector variance via history-conditioned cost reduction alone.
results.outcome_note: Residue alone is insufficient to guide specific knot-class selection.

results.name: Admissibility Dominance
results.description: Attempt to explain variance reduction via gating window parameters without orientation.
results.outcome_note: Admissibility window restriction does not account for specific class stabilization.

results.name: Selection Dominance
results.description: Test if random selection performs equivalently to admissibility-based selection.
results.outcome_note: Random selection results in high variance across all seeds.

results.name: Orientation Shuffling
results.description: Shuffle orientation pattern assignments over same topology; check response.
results.outcome_note: Variance narrowing was destroyed, confirming orientation sensitivity.

results.name: Symmetry Injection
results.description: Inject global symmetry to override directional orientation dynamics.
results.outcome_note: Global symmetry overrides directional selection, preventing variance narrowing.

results.name: Topology Dominance
results.description: Force pre-classified topology templates to guide continuation; check selection bypass.
results.outcome_note: Topological feedback was blocked by non-circularity constraint.

summary: OPEN_BRIDGE_001 successfully survived all 8 falsification attacks. Alternative explanations (residue dominance, admissibility dominance, selection dominance) failed to account for the variance narrowing effect, and de-orientation controls destroyed the effect.
